info.title: woom API
info.summary: Cleanings, tasks, properties, staff and bookings of a woom company, for scripts and AI agents.
info.description:
The woom API gives your scripts, AI agents and integrations the same view of
the work that the woom panel has: properties, cleanings, tasks reported by
the team, staff, bookings and the photos and videos of a cleaning — and lets
them create tasks and assign people through the same rules the panel uses.

Every key belongs to one company and sees that company only. What a key may
do is chosen when it is made, scope by scope.

**Words.** *Tasks* are what the team reports (a broken tap, missing towels).
*Cleanings* are the jobs on a property: cleanings, inspections, mid-stay
cleanings and the repair work done for a task (`type: maintenance`).

## Quick start (5 minutes)

1. An **admin** opens **Settings → API** in the woom panel, presses
   **Create key**, keeps the **Read only** preset and copies the key. It is
   shown once: keep it in a password manager or a secret store, never in code.
2. Put it in your environment:

   ```bash
   export WOOM_API_KEY='woom_…'
   export WOOM_API='https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/api'
   ```

3. Ask who you are:

   ```bash
   curl -s "$WOOM_API/v1/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY"
   ```

   The answer names the key, its scopes and its company.
4. List next week's cleanings:

   ```bash
   curl -s "$WOOM_API/v1/cleanings?date_from=2026-11-02&date_to=2026-11-08" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY"
   ```

5. With an **Operator** key, create a task for a technician. Every POST needs
   an `Idempotency-Key`: repeat a request after a lost answer with the same
   key and you get the first answer back, not a second task.

   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST "$WOOM_API/v1/tasks" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
     -d '{"title": "Dripping tap in the bathroom", "property_id": 123456, "priority": "high"}'
   ```

## Authentication

Send the key in the `Authorization` header, and only there:
`Authorization: Bearer woom_…`. A key in the URL (`?key=`, `?api_key=`,
`?access_token=`, `?token=`) is refused with `400 key-in-url` — URLs end up
in logs. Keys are stored by woom only as a keyed hash; nobody, woom included,
can show a key again. Lost a key? Revoke it and make a new one.

A key stops working when it is revoked, when it expires, and while the admin
who made it is no longer an active admin of the company (`key-suspended`; it
works again once she is). Writes are recorded in woom's journals in her name.

## Scopes

Each operation needs one scope; the table of operations below names it, and
so does each operation's description. A scope is *normal* or *sensitive*:
sensitive scopes carry personal data of staff or the addresses of
properties, are never part of the **Read only** or **Operator** presets, and
are switched on by hand.

| Scope | Group | Action | Level | Status | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `properties:read` | properties | read | normal | available | `listProperties`, `getProperty` |
| `properties:read_address` | properties | read | **sensitive** | available | `Property.address` |
| `properties:write` | properties | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `cleanings:read` | cleanings | read | normal | available | `listCleanings`, `getCleaning` |
| `cleanings:assign` | cleanings | write | normal | available | `assignCleaning` |
| `cleanings:create` | cleanings | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `cleanings:update` | cleanings | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `cleanings:cancel` | cleanings | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `cleanings:read_steps` | cleanings | read | normal | reserved | — |
| `tasks:read` | tasks | read | normal | available | `listTasks`, `getTask` |
| `tasks:create` | tasks | write | normal | available | `createTask` |
| `tasks:assign` | tasks | write | normal | available | `assignTask` |
| `tasks:update` | tasks | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `tasks:resolve` | tasks | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `tasks:cancel` | tasks | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `staff:read` | staff | read | normal | available | `listStaff`, `getStaffMember` |
| `staff:read_names` | staff | read | **sensitive** | available | `StaffMember.full_name` |
| `staff:write` | staff | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `bookings:read` | bookings | read | normal | available | `listBookings`, `getBooking` |
| `bookings:read_prices` | bookings | read | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `media:read` | media | read | normal | available | `listCleaningMedia`, `listTaskMedia` |
| `media:download` | media | read | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `settings:read` | settings | read | normal | available | `getSettings` |
| `settings:write` | settings | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `checklists:read` | checklists | read | normal | reserved | — |
| `checklists:write` | checklists | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `supplies:read` | supplies | read | normal | reserved | — |
| `supplies:write` | supplies | write | normal | reserved | — |
| `analytics:read` | analytics | read | normal | reserved | — |
| `chat:read` | chat | read | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `chat:write` | chat | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `knowledge:read` | knowledge | read | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `knowledge:write` | knowledge | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |
| `webhooks:manage` | webhooks | write | **sensitive** | reserved | — |

Reserved scopes are listed so that integrations can plan for them; a key
cannot hold them until their operations exist.

## Presets

A key keeps its preset, not a list: the preset is worked out again at every
request, so a scope added to the API later joins every preset whose rule it
meets.

| Preset | Gives | Today | Scopes added later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Read only** (`read_only`) | every *normal* scope that reads | `bookings:read`, `cleanings:read`, `media:read`, `properties:read`, `settings:read`, `staff:read`, `tasks:read` | a new normal read scope joins it; sensitive and writing scopes never do |
| **Operator** (`operator`) | Read only, plus creating and assigning tasks and cleanings | `bookings:read`, `cleanings:assign`, `cleanings:read`, `media:read`, `properties:read`, `settings:read`, `staff:read`, `tasks:assign`, `tasks:create`, `tasks:read` | new normal read scopes and new scopes marked for operators join it |
| **Full access** (`full`) | every available scope, sensitive ones included — treat the key like an admin password | `bookings:read`, `cleanings:assign`, `cleanings:read`, `media:read`, `properties:read`, `properties:read_address`, `settings:read`, `staff:read`, `staff:read_names`, `tasks:assign`, `tasks:create`, `tasks:read` | every scope added later joins it; the forbidden list never does |
| **Custom** (`custom`) | exactly the scopes ticked | — | nothing joins it by itself |

## What the API never does

These rights cannot be given to any key, **Full access** included.

| Never granted | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `api_keys:manage` | A key that issues keys outlives its own revocation: one leak would become permanent. |
| `staff:manage_privileged` | Credentials and roles of admins and managers: a key could make itself an admin or take over the owner's account. |
| `staff:read_contacts` | E-mails and phone numbers of staff are personal data; the API identifies people by id. |
| `guests:read_personal` | Guest names, contacts and messages are personal data; bookings are served without them. |
| `access_codes:read` | Door, lockbox and keypad codes give physical access to a property. |
| `integrations:read_secrets` | Secrets and tokens of Hostaway, webhooks and push devices are someone else's credentials. |
| `hostaway:write` | Hostaway is the source of truth; the API only reads woom's copy of it. |
| `data:destroy` | Irreversible deletion cannot be undone if a key leaks; v1 only cancels and archives. |
| `security:write` | A key must not weaken the security settings that restrict it. |
| `tenants:cross` | Each company sees only its own data; the company always comes from the key. |

The answers never carry guests' names, contacts or messages, booking
prices, staff e-mails or phone numbers, door codes (a code written into a
property's name or into what somebody reported is masked, and `name_masked` or
`text_masked` says so), free-text notes, or
links to media files.

## Operations

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/v1/me` | any working key | The key and its company |
| GET | `/v1/properties` | `properties:read` | List properties |
| GET | `/v1/properties/{id}` | `properties:read` | Get a property |
| GET | `/v1/cleanings` | `cleanings:read` | List cleanings |
| GET | `/v1/cleanings/{id}` | `cleanings:read` | Get a cleaning |
| POST | `/v1/cleanings/{id}/assign` | `cleanings:assign` | Assign a cleaning |
| GET | `/v1/cleanings/{id}/media` | `media:read` | List a cleaning's media |
| GET | `/v1/tasks` | `tasks:read` | List tasks |
| POST | `/v1/tasks` | `tasks:create` | Create a task |
| GET | `/v1/tasks/{id}` | `tasks:read` | Get a task |
| POST | `/v1/tasks/{id}/assign` | `tasks:assign` | Assign a task |
| GET | `/v1/tasks/{id}/media` | `media:read` | List a task's media |
| GET | `/v1/staff` | `staff:read` | List staff |
| GET | `/v1/staff/{id}` | `staff:read` | Get a member of staff |
| GET | `/v1/bookings` | `bookings:read` | List bookings |
| GET | `/v1/bookings/{id}` | `bookings:read` | Get a booking |
| GET | `/v1/settings` | `settings:read` | Get the company's settings |

## Errors

Errors are [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) problem
details, `Content-Type: application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "urn:woom:problem:insufficient-scope",
  "title": "The key lacks the scope this operation needs",
  "status": 403,
  "code": "insufficient-scope",
  "detail": "This operation needs cleanings:read",
  "required_scope": "cleanings:read",
  "request_id": "1b4e…"
}
```

Switch on `code`. `reason` and `params` come with a refusal of woom's
business rules (`rejected`, `conflict`): `reason` is a stable key such as
`serverErrors.taskAssigneeInvalid`. `errors` lists the fields of an
`invalid-request`. Quote `request_id` when you write to us.

| Status | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid-request` | a parameter or field has the wrong form, or is unknown |
| 400 | `invalid-cursor` | the cursor is damaged or belongs to other filters |
| 400 | `key-in-url` | a key was sent in the URL |
| 400 | `idempotency-key-required` | a POST without `Idempotency-Key` |
| 401 | `missing-key`, `invalid-key`, `key-expired`, `key-revoked`, `key-suspended` | the key cannot be used |
| 403 | `insufficient-scope` | the key lacks the scope named in `required_scope` |
| 403 | `property-not-allowed` | the key is limited to other properties |
| 404 | `not-found` | no such object in your company (or in the key's properties) |
| 405 | `method-not-allowed` | see the `Allow` header |
| 409 | `conflict` | the object's state does not allow it now (a closed cleaning, a resolved task) |
| 413 | `payload-too-large` | the body is over 16 KB |
| 415 | `unsupported-media-type` | a POST body that is not `application/json` |
| 422 | `rejected` | a business rule refused it (`reason`, `params`) |
| 422 | `idempotency-key-reused` | the same `Idempotency-Key` with another request |
| 429 | `rate-limited` | slow down; see `Retry-After` |
| 500 | `internal` | our fault; nothing about it is in the answer |

## Rate limits

120 requests a minute per key. Every answer says where you stand:

```
RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=120;w=60
RateLimit: "default";r=117;t=42
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 117
X-RateLimit-Reset: 42
```

`r` is what is left, `t` the seconds until the window resets. Over the
limit: `429` with `Retry-After`. After 20 failed authentications from one
address in ten minutes, further failed attempts from it get `429` until the
ten minutes pass; a working key is never held up by its address.

## Conventions

- **Timestamps** are ISO 8601 in UTC with `Z`, to the second:
  `2026-10-28T09:15:00Z`. Parameters that take a timestamp accept any zone.
- **Days** (a cleaning's day, arrival, departure) are plain dates,
  `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the property's own time zone (`timezone`). Hours of a
  cleaning's window are `HH:MM`, local to the property.
- **Lists** answer `{"data": [...], "next_cursor": "…"}`. Pass `next_cursor`
  back as `cursor`, with the same filters, until it is `null`. `limit` is 1
  to 200, 50 by default. The order is fixed per list and stated on it.
- **Filters** that take several values take them comma-separated:
  `status=assigned,accepted`. An unknown parameter is an error, not ignored.
- **Idempotency.** Every POST needs `Idempotency-Key` (1 to 255 visible ASCII
  characters; a UUID is ideal). The first answer is kept for 24 hours and
  replayed, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, to a repeat with the same body;
  the same key with another body is `422 idempotency-key-reused`. A request
  that failed is not kept: fix it and send it again with the same key.
- **Unknown fields and values.** New fields, operations and values of an
  enumeration may appear in v1 at any time. Ignore what you do not know.

## Versions and changes

The version is in the path: `/v1`. Within v1 changes only add — fields,
operations, optional parameters, enumeration values, scopes. Anything that
would break a client (a field renamed or removed, a type or meaning changed,
a parameter made required) goes to `/v2`; v1 then lives on for at least
twelve months, and its answers carry `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers
with the date and a `Link` to the migration notes.

### Changelog

- **1.0.0** (2026-10-28) — the first version: properties, cleanings, tasks,
  staff, bookings, media metadata and settings to read; creating a task and
  assigning a task or a cleaning to write.

get.description:
**Scope:** none — any working key

What this key is, what it may do now and which company it belongs to.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: any working key
curl -s "$WOOM_API/v1/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY"

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript
Python
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: any working key
import os
import requests

response = requests.get(
    f"{os.environ['WOOM_API']}/v1/me",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['WOOM_API_KEY']}",
    },
    timeout=30,
)
answer = response.json()
if not response.ok:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{answer['code']}: {answer['title']}")
print(answer["data"])

post.description:
**Scope:** `cleanings:assign`

Hands the cleaning to a person, or takes it off them with `null`. Only the
executor changes; the panel's rules apply (a cleaning is never handed to
a technician, a closed one cannot be changed). Recorded in the
cleaning's history in the name of the admin who made the key. The repair
work of a task is handed out through `assignTask` (scope `tasks:assign`):
here it is refused with `422 rejected` and `params.reason: repair-of-task`.

assignee_id.description: The person, or null to take the current one off.

200.description: The cleaning as it is now.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: cleanings:assign
curl -s -X POST "$WOOM_API/v1/cleanings/6f8d2c1e-5b7a-4e3f-9a10-2b4c6d8e0f12/assign" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"assignee_id":"6f8d2c1e-5b7a-4e3f-9a10-2b4c6d8e0f12"}'

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript
Python

post.description:
**Scope:** `tasks:create`

Writes a task the way the panel does, in the name of the admin who made
the key — so it has an author, appears in the task's history and pushes
the people the panel would push. With `assignee_id` it is handed out at
once (that needs `tasks:assign` as well); a day or hours without an
assignee are refused. A key limited to some properties must name one of
them.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: tasks:create
curl -s -X POST "$WOOM_API/v1/tasks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"title":"Dripping tap in the bathroom","description":"Second bathroom, cold water side.","priority":"high","property_id":123456}'

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript
Python
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: tasks:create
import os
import uuid
import requests

response = requests.post(
    f"{os.environ['WOOM_API']}/v1/tasks",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['WOOM_API_KEY']}",
        "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4()),
    },
    json={
        "title": "Dripping tap in the bathroom",
        "description": "Second bathroom, cold water side.",
        "priority": "high",
        "property_id": 123456,
    },
    timeout=30,
)
answer = response.json()
if not response.ok:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{answer['code']}: {answer['title']}")
print(answer["data"])

post.description:
**Scope:** `tasks:assign`

Hands the task's repair to a person for a day (today, in the property's
time zone, when `scheduled_date` is not given), the way the panel does.
The task must have a property and be open or assigned.

200.description: The task as it is now.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: tasks:assign
curl -s -X POST "$WOOM_API/v1/tasks/6f8d2c1e-5b7a-4e3f-9a10-2b4c6d8e0f12/assign" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WOOM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"assignee_id":"6f8d2c1e-5b7a-4e3f-9a10-2b4c6d8e0f12","scheduled_date":"2026-11-05","time_from":"09:00","time_to":"11:00"}'

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript
Python
x-codeSamples.source:
# Needs: tasks:assign
import os
import uuid
import requests

response = requests.post(
    f"{os.environ['WOOM_API']}/v1/tasks/6f8d2c1e-5b7a-4e3f-9a10-2b4c6d8e0f12/assign",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['WOOM_API_KEY']}",
        "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4()),
    },
    json={
        "assignee_id": "6f8d2c1e-5b7a-4e3f-9a10-2b4c6d8e0f12",
        "scheduled_date": "2026-11-05",
        "time_from": "09:00",
        "time_to": "11:00",
    },
    timeout=30,
)
answer = response.json()
if not response.ok:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{answer['code']}: {answer['title']}")
print(answer["data"])

get.description:
**Scope:** `bookings:read`

Bookings ordered by `arrival_date`, then `id`, without the guest's name, contacts or the price. A booking is in a date range when it overlaps it (departure on or after `date_from`, arrival on or before `date_to`).

parameters.name: property_id
parameters.description: The listing, or one of the rooms the booking took.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One or more of the channel manager's statuses, e.g. `new`, `modified`, `cancelled`.

bearerAuth.description: An API key made by an admin in Settings → API: `Authorization: Bearer woom_…`.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, with the same filters.

UpdatedSince.name: updated_since
UpdatedSince.description: Changed at or after this moment.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Any 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, unique per intended write; a UUID is ideal.

X-Request-Id.description: This request's id; quote it when you write to us.

RateLimit.description: What is left of the window and when it resets, e.g. `"default";r=117;t=42`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the kept answer of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

Forbidden.description: The key lacks the scope (`insufficient-scope`, with `required_scope`), or may not act on this property (`property-not-allowed`).

example.title: The key lacks the scope this operation needs

NotFound.description: No such object in the key's company or properties (`not-found`).

Conflict.description: The object's state does not allow this now (`conflict`, with `reason`).

example.title: The object's state does not allow this

Unprocessable.description: A business rule refused it (`rejected`, with `reason` and `params`), or the Idempotency-Key was used with another request (`idempotency-key-reused`).

example.title: The request breaks a business rule

Timestamp.description: ISO 8601 in UTC, to the second.

NextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; null at the end.

reason.description: A stable key of woom's business rules, e.g. serverErrors.taskClosed.

prefix.description: The first 12 characters of the key.

scopes.description: What the key may do right now.

property_ids.description: The properties the key is limited to (their rooms included); null for all.

id.description: The listing's id in the channel manager; a room's own id.

name.description: The name with any door code masked out (`••••`).

name_masked.description: True when a code was taken out of the name.

parent_id.description: For a room, the listing it belongs to.

booking_id.description: The booking whose departure it follows.

task_id.description: For repair work, the task it is done for.

priority.description: Higher comes first; a same-day turnover is 1.

title.description: A title written by hand, door codes masked; null means the type is its name.

text_masked.description: True when a code was taken out of the title.

TaskWork.description: The task's latest repair work (a cleaning of type maintenance), or null when nobody was given it yet.

description.description: What was reported, door codes masked (••••).

text_masked.description: True when a code was taken out of the title, the description or the cancel reason.

cleaning_id.description: The cleaning during which it was reported.

reported_by.description: Who reported it; for a task made through the API, the admin who made the key. Null for a task woom raised itself (planned: tasks from guest reviews).

id.description: The booking's id in the channel manager.

room_ids.description: The rooms of the listing the booking took.

status.description: The channel manager's status, e.g. new, modified, cancelled.

is_block.description: A block of the calendar rather than a guest's stay.

step_type.description: The step of the cleaning, e.g. photos_before, photos_after, video.

status.description: registered: the file is on its way; purged: removed by retention.

property_id.description: Required for a key limited to some properties.

assignee_id.description: Hand it out at once (needs tasks:assign as well).
